design:
Replica Topology and Persistence: On-demand repository materialization — A host reconstructs an absent repository locally from durable log state when requests require it.
Repository Service Scaling: Explicit repository registration — Users register repositories to activate local configuration and background performance maintenance.
Repository Storage Representation: Delta-compressed packfile storage — Stores most packfile objects as deltas to reduce storage size at the cost of additional read hops.

Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Incremental bounded pack repacking — Small pack batches are rewritten incrementally to control client repository maintenance cost.
Repository Storage Representation: Filesystem-level repository distribution — Repositories are distributed through the filesystem layer to scale application instances without changing Rails or Git internals.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Cross-rack replica placement — Replicas are distributed across racks to survive rack-level failures as well as individual node failures.
Repository Service Scaling: Quiesced rolling server reboot — Servers finish in-progress reads, exclude new reads, and restart sequentially within bounded failure domains.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Compressed Git index — Index compression reduces client-side repository metadata size.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Incremental reachable-commit graph — Split incremental commit-graph files include reachable commits while limiting repeated update cost.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Synchronous write commitment — A write is accepted only after synchronous commitment establishes the durability promise.
Repository Storage Representation: Packfile-based Git networking — Uses Git packfiles as the client-server transfer representation regardless of internal server storage.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Disk repository warm cache — Local disk repositories serve as reconstructible caches rather than fixed authoritative placement.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Rails monolith — The application begins and largely remains a Rails monolith around repository access.
Repository Storage Representation: Centralized repository hosting — A centralized service provides the primary repository access point despite Git's distributed capabilities.

Repository Service Scaling: Three-replica repository topology — Each repository receives at least three copies to provide redundancy and capacity for continued operation after one machine failure.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Two-phase repack and expire — Pack rewriting and obsolete-pack deletion run as separate maintenance operations.

Repository Service Scaling: Quiesced read admission — Withdraw a planned-maintenance server from new reads while allowing existing reads to drain.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Small-pack batch selection — Each incremental repack selects a bounded set of small packfiles.
Repository Storage Representation: Application layer over unmodified Git — Hosting features are built above standard Git repositories without maintaining a Git fork.

Replica Topology and Persistence: GVFS deployment without cache infrastructure — Whether GVFS is deployed without the cache-server infrastructure required for sufficiently large repositories.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Majority-exclusive write locking — Each write locks a majority exclusively so conflicting writes cannot both acquire a majority simultaneously.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Arbitrary replica-based read scaling — Read replicas can be deployed in arbitrary numbers to scale read-only operations.
Repository Service Scaling: Priority scheduling for user updates — User-initiated reference updates take priority over maintenance bookkeeping.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Atomic reference-update rollback — Failed tentative reference transactions are rolled back in full.

Replica Topology and Persistence: S3 Express object-storage substrate — A low-latency object-storage tier is selected for high-throughput WAL persistence.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Consistency and partition tolerance priority — The system prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance over availability when those qualities conflict.
Repository Storage Representation: Centralized repository hosting — A centralized service provides the primary repository access point despite Git's distributed capabilities.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Disk repository warm cache — Local disk repositories serve as reconstructible caches rather than fixed authoritative placement.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Rails monolith — The application begins and largely remains a Rails monolith around repository access.

Repository Service Scaling: Migration-friendly repository platform — Provides a low-friction path for moving repositories onto the hosting platform.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Background Git object-database maintenance — Expensive object-database cleanup runs in the background instead of blocking routine commands.
Write Commitment and Consistency: WAL durability before push acknowledgement — Require durable operation-log persistence before reporting a successful push to the client.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Co-located filesystem replica placement — Keeps filesystem replicas adjacent to control replication latency, rather than separating them across racks or sites.
Repository Service Scaling: Checksum-guided repository repair scheduling — Detect damaged repository copies quickly and schedule repair work using continuously tracked validity state.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Consensus-free arbitrary repository primaries — Any healthy server may accept a push without election because durable compare-and-swap synchronization makes concurrent updates safe.

Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Built-in filesystem monitor — Git's filesystem monitor accelerates status and add operations in repositories with many working-tree files.
Repository Storage Representation: Git-level distribution — Repository distribution modifies or distributes Git itself rather than replicating repository data above it.

Repository Service Scaling: Core Git upstreaming — Performance capabilities are implemented in and contributed to core Git so specialized-client dependencies can eventually be removed.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Single-pack full repacking — Rewriting all repository objects into one consolidated pack-file during maintenance.

Write Commitment and Consistency: Permanent data-loss resistance — Accepted pushes, merges, edits, and repository creations must not be corrupted or reverted.

Replica Topology and Persistence: Proxy-mediated repository replication — A proxy transparently forwards each Git push to multiple repository replicas.
Repository Service Scaling: Three-failure offline threshold — A node is advisory-offline after approximately three consecutive failed operations.
Write Commitment and Consistency: JGit repository-storage abstraction — Uses replaceable JGit storage interfaces to change repository storage while retaining Git operations.

Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Non-virtualized large-repository support — Scaling very large repositories with Git and client optimizations without requiring a virtualized filesystem.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Deterministic replica transaction results — Replica transaction evaluation produces deterministic reference-update results.

Replica Topology and Persistence: ETag-validated replica freshness — Conditional object-store metadata validation confirms replica freshness before serving reads.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: Git-aware custom filesystem watcher — Uses a Git-specific watcher that respects repository exclusions instead of a general-purpose filesystem watcher.

Repository Storage Representation: Object-level repository distribution — Distributes individual content-addressed objects across storage nodes rather than preserving repository-level packfile organization.

Write Commitment and Consistency: Linearized repository operations — Process pushes and fundamental repository operations in one consistent order.

Repository Service Scaling: Co-located transfer cache proxy — Proxy large-repository object requests through cache servers near users and build machines.
Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling: GVFS protocol standardization — The GVFS protocol is made a standard feature of the core Git client.

Repository Service Scaling: Foreground automatic garbage collection — Runs repository garbage collection synchronously at command completion or threshold triggers.
Write Commitment and Consistency: Automatic replica repair — Unhealthy or lagging replicas are repaired automatically to restore redundancy and service capacity.
